Sam —

Appreciate the quick questions. I attached a short trace (trace_snippet.har) that contains a p99 sample and annotated notes. Quick answers inline: 

- p99 spikes: primarily from concurrent long-context (>3k token) summarize+rerank calls. There were only 2 distinct cold-starts during the 30-minute window (scale-up events after a tranche of requests).
- Cold-start mitigation: autoscale warm pools + prefix KV caching reduces cold-start frequency; we recommend pre-warm hooks for your nightly batch jobs to avoid the early-morning spike.
- Model variant fallback: switching to the 13B variant shaves ~40ms off p95 at the expense of ~12% higher per-token compute cost. That tradeoff is predictable and can be automated as part of the routing policy.

Pricing sketch (illustrative, subject to final SOW):
- 8x A100 reserved pool (guaranteed baseline throughput ~700 TPS sustained): 12-month commit = $26,400/month (effective ~18% discount vs on-demand); 24-month commit = $23,500/month (~28% discount).
- Add-on burst capacity (up to +25% throughput) billed at blended rate with short-notice multiplier.
- SLA options: p95 latency credits tiered by severity (example: p95 >250ms for two consecutive weeks -> 5% monthly credit).

If you confirm whether Evergreen wants guaranteed 700 TPS or to aim for 850 TPS (with autoscale and higher commit), I’ll run a counteroffer that includes a final price, SLA credit table, and onboarding credits.

Attaching: trace_snippet.har

Thanks —
Lauren
